Cheating AI Fruit is an AI video trend in which artificial intelligence is used to generate videos about anthropomorphic fruit people cheating on their spouses. The trend began on February 28th, 2026, when TikToker @trombonechef posted the first part in a series of videos about a strawberry woman who cheats on her husband with her eggplant boss. The trend became increasingly popularized throughout March 2026, inspiring similar videos and videos reacting to the memes.

On February 28th, 2026, TikToker[1] @trombonechef posted an AI-generated video about a strawberry woman who cheats on her strawberry husband with her boss, an eggplant. When she goes out to cheat, she claims she's working late. The eggplant gets her pregnant. When the baby is delivered, the strawberry husband notices that the baby is an eggplant and discovers that his wife cheated with her boss. The video gained over 2.9 million views in two weeks.

The TikToker[2] continued posting videos following the same plot line between late February 2026 and mid-March.

The second part, uploaded on March 1st, 2026, garnered over 24 million views in two weeks. In the video, the strawberry man decides to leave his wife after finding an orange woman to have an affair with. He marries the orange woman within two days, then returns home and kicks out his strawberry wife and eggplant baby, leaving them homeless.

On March 2nd, the TikToker[3] uploaded the third part of the series, gaining over 4.9 million views in two weeks. In the video, the strawberry man and his orange wife grow closer and plan to have a baby. The strawberry woman asks the boss, her baby's dad, to help out, but he won't. Strawberry woman dedicates her life to hard work to keep her baby fed and buys a gun.

The series continued over the next few weeks, reaching its 12th entry in mid-March 2026.

The AI Fruit videos inspired similar AI-generated videos of fruit cheating on their spouses as the trend garnered virality in early March 2026.

On March 1st, 2026, TikToker[4] @brhealt posted a video where a blueberry woman cheats on her partner with a banana man.

On March 2nd, the same TikToker[5] posted another video of a blueberry woman cheating with a zucchini and having a zucchini baby, garnering over 1.2 million views in two weeks.

title: The EASIEST Boba Recipe you will ever try!! 🧋✨
description:
The EASIEST BOBA RECIPE you will ever try🧋✨ #shorts #boba #recipe #bubbletea #easyrecipe #homecafe
I’ve tried/made so many boba recipes and this one is by far the easiest & beginner-friendly! I hope it’s helpful, let me know if you try it out 💕
✨ RECIPE ✨
1. Melt a melona ice cream bar naturally, do not heat it to melt. Yes, you can use other ice cream (~75ml or 1/3 cup).
2. After it’s completely melted, mix in 1 tbsp tapioca starch/tapioca flour (they are the same thing) and food coloring (optional).
3. Microwave for 1 min and let cool for 1-2 min.
4. Gradually mix in/knead tapioca starch until it forms a dough that is not sticky to the touch. I usually use around 1 cup, but adjust accordingly.
5. Shape into boba balls (or shape of choice) coat in a little bit of tapioca starch to prevent them from sticking to each other.
6. Boil for 20 minutes, strain, rinse in warm water, and soak in sweetener of choice (I usually just use normal sugar).
7. Enjoy in your drink of choice! I like to have a cup of milk + ice + melona bar of the same flavor so it melts into the milk and matches the flavor profile of the boba :)

Who says one nozzle is enough!? 3D printing with different nozzle sizes
description:
Most people only 3D print with the stock 0.4mm nozzle that came with the printer. Like a camera that comes with a stock lens, there's a lot you can do with it, but there are other options that open up new possibilities.

Use smaller nozzles for tiny details and larger ones for quicker printing. Trouble is that plastic doesn't have enough time to melt, so the larger nozzles will have to be longer as well, with longer heating blocks.

New hotends are coming out every day with improved melting capabilities, optimized for higher temperatures, or with other cool tweaks. But E3D's open sourced V6 hotend is still one of the best in terms of value. They've then expanded the options to the Volcano and the SuperVolcano hotends for more and more throughput.

Larger nozzles do have a downside: they can't print small details. So it's not a one size fits all kind of scenario. It's a matter of using the right nozzle for the job. 3D printing is awesome!
